title: Front Disc Brake: Diagnostic Starting Point
introduction:
Front disc brakes turn hydraulic pressure into pad pressure against the rotating discs. Friction slows the wheels and produces heat—the discs have a demanding second job as heat handlers.

I start by describing the concern: noise, pedal feel, pulling, drag or vibration, including when it happens. That description helps direct diagnosis; it does not identify a failed part. Different Mustang brake packages use different calipers and pads, so identify the installed package and piston count before choosing removal instructions or torque values. This page directs you to the brake-system diagnostic procedure; it contains no test setup, measurements or result branches and is not a standalone diagnostic procedure.

edits.text: For front disc brake diagnosis, refer to [Brake System](#/document/G1721936) (206-00 Brake System - General Information, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: The shared diagnostic path connects the reported symptom with the appropriate system checks. Feeling a concern at the front brakes is a starting observation, not proof that the front friction components caused it.
